Bug_Title: "Object.wait()", "Object.notify()" and "Object.notifyAll()" should only be called from synchronized code
Bug_Details:
The Object.wait(…​) , Object.notify() and Object.notifyAll() methods are used in multithreaded environments
to coordinate interdependent tasks that are performed by different threads. These methods are not thread-safe and by contract, they require the
invoking Thread to own the object’s monitor. If a thread invokes one of these methods without owning the object’s monitor an IllegalMonitorStateException is thrown.
Bug_Explanation: The wait() and notify()/notifyAll() methods are called from a non-synchronized block, causing an IllegalMonitorStateException.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered by calling the'setLock' method on an instance of the BugDemo class from a different thread while the'showBug' method is still executing. The'setLock' method attempts to modify the 'isLocked' field, which is guarded by the 'lock' object's monitor, but it is called from a different thread.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results confirm the presence of the bug. The IllegalMonitorStateException is thrown when the thread that is not the owner of the object's monitor tries to call the wait(), notify(), or notifyAll() methods. In this case, the thread that calls the setLock(true) method does not own the monitor of the lock object, hence the IllegalMonitorStateException is thrown.
